answer: A harbour economy stays honest when each agent's standing rests on an anchor record in a mirror ledger on an island. Registration requires reconciling its ledger against that mirror copy in a live sitting with its keeper, who closes one ledger per epoch. A second identity must reconcile two more island ledgers, a third three more, so each new fake costs more than the last. Twenty invented agents would owe 210 reconciliations. Bulk farming fails because sittings cannot be bought in bulk and one operator cannot attend 210 at once, like a sailor checking two mirrors in two harbours at once.
